replacement: “Do you want me to bow down to you, monk?” said Father Ferapont. “Get up!”
“I’ve been to your Sylvester’s. I used to stay there. Is Sylvester well?”
“Red is better. A white one makes me look like I’m in the hospital,” he pronounced pompously. “Well, how are things over there? How’s your elder?”

“He doesn’t ask for money, it’s true, but he’ll not get a farthing out of me all the same. I mean to live as long as I can, you may as well know, my dear Alexey Fyodorovitch, and so I need every farthing, and the longer I live, the more I’ll need,” he went on, pacing from one corner of the room to the other, his hands in the pockets of his loose, greasy overcoat of yellow cotton. “I can still pass for a man of fifty-five, but I want to go on passing for one another twenty years. The older I get, you know, the less pretty I’ll be. The wenches won’t come to me of their own accord, so I’ll need my money. That’s why I’m saving up more and more, just for myself, my dear son Alexey Fyodorovitch. You may as well know that. Because I mean to go on sinning to the end, let me tell you. Sin is sweet. Everybody curses it, and everybody lives in it, only the others do it on the sly and I do it in the open. And that’s why all the other sinners jump on me, for being so simple. And your paradise, Alexey Fyodorovitch, isn’t to my taste, let me tell you. It’s no place for a gentleman, your paradise, even if there is such a thing. I believe I fall asleep and never wake up, and that’s the end of it. You can pray for my soul if you like. If you don’t want to, then don’t, damn you! That’s my philosophy. Ivan spoke well here yesterday, though we were all drunk. Ivan is a conceited coxcomb, but he has no great learning ... no education either. He sits there silent, smiling at you and saying nothing—that’s what gets him by.”
“How cross you are! It’s because of yesterday. You had better lie down,” said Alyosha.

Alyosha felt painfully that since yesterday both of the rivals had found new strength, and their hearts had hardened again. “Father is spiteful and angry. He’s made some plan and he’ll stick to it. And what about Dmitri? He’ll be harder than he was yesterday too. He must be spiteful and angry as well, and no doubt he’s made a plan of his own. Oh, I must find him today, whatever happens.”
“All right, I’m going,” said Alyosha. “Only I don’t know you, and I don’t tease you. They told me how they tease you, but I don’t want to tease you. Good-by!”
